To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the axial compression stiffness of ITER-TF conductors is lower than expected, and that the lower the twist pitch of the cable, the higher the compression yield strength.

the axial compression stiffness of the ITER-TF conductor samples is independent of the constituents of the conductor, the void fraction and the twist pitch of the strands and that cracks are initiated in the cable at small compression levels during cooling from reaction temperature to room and helium temperatures.
the stiffness of the cable of the TFMC is 10 times lower than that of the jacket and the stiffness of the jacket of the TF Coil conductors remains the same as that of TFMC.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development and application of methods for the determination of the mechanical properties of the ITER TF Conductor and the development of a model for the mechanical behaviour of the cable inside the stainless steel tube.
the axial stiffness of the ITER-TF conductor and the effect of the void fraction on the stiffness.
the mechanical properties of the ITER TF conductor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the axial compression tests of the ITER TF conductor samples show that the axial compression stiffness is in the order of 1/5 of that calculated for fully bonded constituents, but that this is not a function of the void fraction.
the axial stiffness of ITER TF Coil conductor is not influenced by void fraction, the constituents and the heat treatment, but by the twist pitch.
the stiffness is not only determined by the void fraction, but also by the type of the cable and its manufacturing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we found that the axial stiffness of the cable inside the jacket is not affected by the reaction and that the axial compression strength is reduced by the cracks in the cable.
the axial stiffness of the TFMC conductor and ITER-TF conductor samples are similar and that cracks occur already during cool down from room to helium temperature.
the axial stiffness of the ITER-TF conductor is mainly determined by the jacket, and the cable is not contributing much to the stiffness of the whole conductor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the axial stiffness of the ITER conductor is not affected by the void fraction.
the ITER TF conductor has a low axial stiffness and is very sensitive to axial compressive loads.
the axial compression stiffness of the ITER conductor is much smaller than that of a fully bonded conductor and that it is independent of the constituents and void fraction.
